entries.description: JSON input is one RFC 8259 value, encoded in UTF-8 without a byte order mark, that uses none of the constants NaN, Infinity and -Infinity and whose strings and member names hold only Unicode scalar values that are not noncharacters.
JSON input contains no duplicate object member names at any depth.
JSON input obeys the ECL restricted-number profile and excludes floats, negative zero, and unsafe integers.
An object contains no duplicate extension identifier and version pair.
An object carries each extension identifier at one version only, unless the registry entry of that identifier sets composable_versions to true; a version the consumer does not know still counts.
A consumer rejects every critical extension that is unknown to it: one without an active registry entry of its identifier and version that the consumer implements (XR1-006).
A message or event does not reference itself as a causal predecessor.
An expiry time is strictly later than the corresponding issue or validity start time.
An admit decision carries an authorization object with its identifier, audience, scope digest, validity interval and use policy, which DCMP2-044 to DCMP2-050 bind to the request.
Deny, hold, and challenge outcomes do not issue executable authority.

An execution_terminal event carries a terminal execution outcome or a non-execution terminal disposition, an event of another type carries neither, and an uncertain terminal outcome keeps its side effects and residual state.
Redaction and supersession reference the derived artifact, and redaction also its redaction manifest.
Integrity thresholds, required signers, accepted suites, and the required flag are mutually consistent.
A bundle does not contain multiple records with the same immutable object identity.
Every local causal predecessor reference binds the predecessor's recomputed canonical digest.
Causal predecessors in one sequence domain, the workflow that workflow.workflow_id names, have lower authenticated sequence values than their successors.
The bundle's local causal graph is acyclic.

Each causal predecessor that the bundle holds has its successor's root trace, and is in its successor's workflow, with an attempt no greater than the successor's, or in the workflow that the successor names as its parent.
The states of each execution attempt, in sequence order, follow the transition table of EBMP2-065, so that no state moves backward and none follows a terminal state.

A native adapter binding meets the nine conditions of EBMP2-069: its body digest and its identity, distinct derived objects with the media types their protocols name, each source field accounted once, a loss class that follows from the dispositions, target paths that name a derived object, exact responsibility coverage, and the fail-closed authority boundary.
A dependency that supplies required proof declares a loss disposition that fails closed, one of the three that TS1-032 lists: fail_closed, quarantine or emergency_halt.

A safe-state profile that lists STRICT-FAILURE-1 in claimed_profiles declares no fail_open disposition for a dependency, an action class or its evidence buffer; the profile identifier and name decide nothing.
An extension identifier in the ecl.* namespace is allocated in the consumer's registry snapshot, whatever its criticality.
In-band decision-request parameters have the ecl.digest.sha-256.v1 digest of their restricted canonical JSON as parameters_digest.
A decision request's action.budget_debit.amount is written without a sign, so that no declared debit is negative.
A halt or quarantine control message declares the emergency control plane in its authority context.
An event record's event kind, and for authority and execution events its state, is the one its event_type requires.
The value of an extension whose registry entry names a value schema validates against that schema.
An admit response carries only permitting consequence-coupling results: budget authorized, witness satisfied, quorum met, and no blocker reason.
A human approval or rejection that records its presentation is decided no sooner than the minimum review time after that presentation.
A recorded control change names approvers other than its requester, and a change that disables, bypasses or automates approval of a control expires after it takes effect.

A response that records its decision basis lists each input once, input names compared after the case normalization of RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.1 and RFC 8141 section 3.1; cites no actor_supplied or judgment input, and no input that was not available or was computed from one that was not, as supporting it; records no input computed from an input that is not verifiable as verifiable; and has no input computed from itself, directly or through other inputs. An admit cites at least one verifiable input as supporting it and no required input that was not available or was computed from one that was not. The outcome is no less strict than a recorded verifiable-only outcome; while that outcome is not admit, no input supports the outcome, and when it is admit, a verifiable input supports it and no required verifiable input was not available. No input obtained after the decision is recorded as available, and no value describes a time after the decision or after the input was obtained; a record that gives when an input was obtained gives when the request was received, no later than the decision, and a record that gives when the request was received gives both times of each available input. A verifier that holds the request refuses an input recorded as verifiable whose source is the request's actor, and a request received before it was issued. Each decision response that an AARM, ACS or MCP exchange record holds carries exactly one decision basis and is checked with the request the record holds.
Each decision response in the evidence of a decision carries its decision basis in ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1.

A decision basis that a verifier checks against a register it holds names that register version and lists exactly the inputs that the register declares for the request's action class, each once, with the declared class, required flag, derived_from and source, the source compared as input names are; and no input recorded as available was obtained more than its declared deadline after the request was received or has a value older than its declared maximum age at the time of the decision.

A Consequential Action Register declares each action class once and each decision input of a class once, input names compared as DCMP2-053 compares them; each name in a declaration's derived_from is another input declared for the same class; no input declared verifiable is computed from one that is not; and no input is computed from itself, directly or through other inputs.

A MODIFY releases nothing under the original request: the modified action, if it goes ahead, is a new decision request for the original's operation, target, action class, risk class, actor and subject carrying the modified parameters as the same JSON values, linked to the original by ecl.relation.modification-of.v1, and released only under its own admit; a MODIFY whose record holds neither a new request nor a release is a deny of the original; a decision that is not a modification has no new request.
A hold or challenge mapped from DEFER or STEP_UP expires no later than the AARM deadline, into a safe state that permits no new effect.

AARM R2, R3 and R7 outputs, and every AARM output in the judgment-source role, are judgment inputs in every decision basis that the record holds, the modification response's included; the judgment-source role lists the AARM decision exactly once as an R4 input; and an admit rests on verifiable inputs only.
The ECL outcome is no weaker than the outcome the AARM decision maps to.
An action released under the AARM binding has a DCMP-2 admit bound to the exact request, and is released within the authorization's window with the admitted parameters.
An AARM receipt is bound to the execution_terminal event of its action by identifier, RFC 8785 digest and decision, and records the parameters of the request it governed.

The inputs of an AARM exchange record are the entries of the decision basis that its decision response records in ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, each once and equal to its entry apart from the AARM requirement it names; the decision basis of the modification response carries the same register reference, member for member, and records the same inputs with the same declarations.
A claim negotiates on_decision_failure deny, and a Guardian decision failure ends in neither an admit nor a release.
The ECL response to an ask or defer expires no later than the Guardian's deadline, into a safe state that permits no new effect, and nothing is released after it expires.

A modify releases nothing under the original request: the action it produces, if it goes ahead, is a new decision request for the original's operation, target, action class, risk class, actor and subject with the effective parameters as the same JSON values, linked by ecl.relation.modification-of.v1, and an unusable modifications object gets no new request; a modify whose record holds neither a new request nor a release is a deny of the original; a decision that is not a modification, or a decision failure, has no new request.

A Guardian decision from an agent or composite evaluator, or from an evaluator that is not stated, is a judgment input; a deterministic Guardian decision that a hook point carried to the decision point is actor_supplied; any other takes the least trusted class of the inputs its request carried and is verifiable only when the record names them; the Guardian decision has that class in every decision basis that the record holds, the modification response's included; a response that records the Guardian decision has exactly one input marked as it; and an admit rests on verifiable inputs only.
The ECL outcome is no weaker than the outcome the Guardian's disposition maps to.
An action released at an ACS hook point has a DCMP-2 admit bound to the exact request, and is released within the authorization's window with the admitted parameters.
The ECL response records the Guardian decision it depends on in ecl.ext.acs-decision.v1, and each recorded chain head is the head of the recomputed ACS session chain after that step.

The inputs of an ACS exchange record that holds a decision response are the entries of the decision basis that the response records in ecl.ext.decision-basis.v1, each once and equal to its entry apart from the Guardian marker; the decision basis of the modification response carries the same register reference, member for member, and records the same inputs with the same declarations.
An MCP gateway that asked for a decision forwards nothing when the decision service is unavailable or answers with no verified decision.
An MCP gateway forwards only a request whose method is mapped, a call only to a mapped tool, and only when the tool's definition and server identity are those the mapping reviewed.

An MCP gateway's decision request takes its action class, operation, target, risk class and evidence profile from the mapping, its parameters from the call's arguments read from their RFC 8785 form, and carries the critical ecl.ext.mcp-binding.v1 naming them and the digest of the call's complete params; a call with a member other than jsonrpc, id, method and params, or whose id or params holds a number of magnitude greater than 2^53 - 1, gets no decision request.

An MCP gateway forwards a request only on a verified admit bound to its decision request, within the authorization's window and uses, at a final observation that the release guard places before the window's end and that the release event records, with a send that completed before the window's end, and forwards exactly the call that the admitted request binds: its method, tool, arguments, input responses and request state, a params object with the digest that the admitted request carries, and no member added or removed.

An MCP gateway forwards on an admit that leaves obligations to Enforcement before the release, each obligation whose satisfaction is before_release and each state witness that the admit defers, only on an execution_released event that records in ecl.ext.obligation-discharge.v1 a discharge of each of them as satisfied, with no entry that names an obligation the admit does not carry or that another entry names, and that the record's obligation_discharge repeats.

A request an MCP gateway does not forward gets the JSON-RPC error that the profile's error table gives for the first cause that holds, in the order of MG1-006, an unproven pre-release obligation and an evidence log that cannot record the release among them, and never a result.

The evidence of a forwarded MCP request binds the server's response by RFC 8785 digest, records the state that response reads as and the forward's completion, and the governed AI system receives that response, with the code of a server error that uses one of the error table's codes replaced by -32603; a refused request is recorded in a non-release state, or as cancelled when its authorization was consumed, and a recovered exchange claims only the outcome that the gateway's journal shows.
An exporter reads an object no earlier than its time, and the evidence is the same after an export, failed or not.

An exported log record's event name, time and table attributes are those of the object it copies, its observed time is not earlier than the object's time, it carries no digest that can be computed without the export key, and with an export key it names the key and carries the object's keyed digest.

An exported log record carries no attribute outside the attribute table, no identifier of a person or record that the table exports only when declared, and no body, unless the export policy declares it.
An exported log record's SeverityNumber is the one the severity table gives for the object, and its SeverityText is that number's short name.
An access token is issued only for a verified admit, and its ECL authorization_details entry, audience, validity, subject, actor and confirmation key express that admit.

A resource server accepts a token only when every segment reads under the strict JSON profile, it verifies under a configured issuer key with an allowed asymmetric algorithm and no header key, unknown kid or crit member, and its iss is the configured issuer.

A resource server accepts a presentation only for its own audience, within the token's validity with the declared clock-skew allowance and within its entry's window, with a valid proof of possession, for the entry's target, operation and parameter digest, and within its uses.
A resource server that refuses a presentation names the code that the presentation table gives for the first check the presentation fails.

An execution_released event whose decision response carries an obligation to be met before release, or a witness result required before release, records in ecl.ext.obligation-discharge.v1 a discharge of each such obligation, recorded as satisfied with a proof reference and digest and checked no later than the release was observed; no entry names an obligation that the response does not carry, names one twice, was checked before the decision was issued, has a proof obtained after it was checked, or names an object of the bundle by another digest. A proof that is an ECL object is carried in the bundle as its own object and checked there, each failure reported with ecl.error.obligation-unproven.v1: a valid envelope under the trust policy, signed by the issuer the obligation names and never by the requesting actor, of a type the obligation admits, bound to this exchange and fresh at the release.
